structure: M-outer over 2-level (m_hi,m_lo) M-index (8x4=32 tiles, nested affine_range); identity-transpose shared lhs_t=[k_in,m_in]; a resident in SBUF; down-projection tT=(x@a)^T=[R,m_in] zero-init PSUM K-accumulate then fp32 copy to SBUF before N loop; per n-tile (96 of width 128) base x@w K-accumulated into one PSUM bank then low-rank (x@a)@b=tT.T@b FUSED into the SAME bank before one copy+store to v5[m_hi,m_lo,:,nt,:]
notes: First correct lora kernel (phase 1). Pure fp32, fused single-bank low-rank residual (no HBM round-trip for (x@a) or (x@a)@b). Host-side runs/_layout_check.py passes (worst fused tile rel-L2 4.9e-7). all_seeds_passed=False in the profiler dump is the benign allclose field NKIBench does NOT gate on; l2_norm_passed=True on all 5 seeds is the gate (verify.py PASS). Slower than baseline (0.382x) as expected -- phase-1 has no speed target. Phase-2 levers (N_CHUNK=512 strided store, resident b, M-blocking to amortize the per-M-tile w+b reload driving HBMrd=7813MB, bf16x2 split) deferred.

structure: fp32 M-block B=4 with the 2-level (m_hi,m_lo) M-index as the natural block/member split: M-block == m_hi (8 blocks), the B=4 members == m_lo (0..3); N_CHUNK=512. Per m_hi block: prologue transposes x per member (identity idiom, shared lhs_t[m_lo,kt]=[k_in,m_in]) and K-accumulates the fp32 down-proj tT[m_lo]=(x@a)^T into a zero-init PSUM bank then copies to SBUF BEFORE the N loop. Per N-chunk (24 of width 512): base x@w K-accumulated into 4 distinct fp32 PSUM banks with each w K-tile [k_in,512] loaded ONCE and reused across the 4 members; then the low-rank (x@a)@b = tT[m_lo].T @ b_chunk FUSED into each member's bank (b_chunk loaded ONCE, reused across the 4 members); 512-wide result stored as 4 sub-tile writes out_sb[:,128j:128j+128] -> v5[m_hi,m_lo,:,4c+j,:], j in 0..3 (static_range).
notes: D1, the phase-2 fp32 fallback. Ports sibling matmul_v2_b4's M-block structure; the base GEMM x@w (96.6% of MACs, shape-identical to the matmul operator) drives the win. HBM read collapsed 7813->2150 MB (3.6x) by loading each w K-tile and b_chunk once per N-chunk and reusing across the 4 members; HBM write byte-identical 201 MB => no spill (AC-2.1). Flipped from DMA-co-saturated (89%) to DMA-idle (33%), now cleanly PE-bound (PE 98%, MFU 48%) = the sibling matmul_v2_b4 fp32 regime (1.017x, MFU 49%, HBMrd 2097 MB). worst rel-L2 4.874e-7 byte-identical to lora_v1 (M-blocking is a pure reschedule of the same fp32 math). Full 5-seed 14.8385ms/0.988x (--fast 1.042x; ~5% fast-vs-full gap per BL-20260709-fast-vs-full-run-latency, full run recorded). 2.6x faster than lora_v1 (38.36ms). Kept as fp32 fallback; D2 bf16x2 base-split is the lever past the fp32 floor. all_seeds_passed=False is the benign server allclose field NKIBench does not gate on.
verdict: fp32-fallback (kept; superseded by D2 bf16x2 split on latency)

seed_caveat: all 5 profiler seeds [0,21,42,63,84] draw the seed-42 input (adapter reseeds np.random.seed(42)), so the on-device 5-seed PASS (worst_rel_l2 6.240e-7) is ONE distinct input; the true distinct-input numeric margin is the offline base-only composite diversity worst 3.934e-7 over seeds [0,21,63,84] (runs/offline_lora_bf16_split_sim.py). Both are reported, never conflated.
structure: Localized diff on D1 (lora_v2_mblk4): base GEMM x@w becomes the compensated bf16x2 3-product split lhs_hi@w_hi + lhs_hi@w_lo + lhs_lo@w_hi (drop lo@lo) into the fp32 PSUM bank; w limbs built per (c,kt) via nl.copy->bf16 + nisa.tensor_tensor subtract into bf16 dest; lhs limbs resident (2xbf16 = D1 fp32 lhs_t bytes). Two guards: (AC-3.1) fp32 down-proj tT_psum += nc_matmul(a_local[kt], lhs_t_f) folded into the transpose/split loop, consuming the transient fp32 lhs_t_f BEFORE the bf16 limbs are built from it and it is freed (no resident fp32 lhs_t); (AC-3.2) tT_psum zeroed once per member and K-accumulated over 40 K-tiles in the prologue only, N-chunk loop reads the completed tT as tT.T@b_chunk (fp32). Down-proj x@a and up-proj (x@a)@b stay fp32. B=4 M-block == m_hi, N_CHUNK=512, 4-sub-tile store, same as D1.
notes: D2, the phase-2 PROMOTED kernel. bf16x2 3-product split on the base GEMM only (96.6% of MACs, shape-identical to the matmul operator; sibling matmul_v3_bf16_split took the same base 1.017x->1.274x). worst rel-L2 6.240e-7 == device quadrature sqrt(fp32_floor 4.874e-7^2 + offline composite bf16 3.93e-7^2) = 6.261e-7 within 0.34%; backed-out bf16 3.897e-7 == offline 3.93e-7 within 0.9% -- the split behaves exactly as the offline sim modeled, the excess over the offline number is the fp32 floor (present in the fp32 kernels too), NOT a compensation bug. TRUE PE-active -27.4% (14.79->10.73ms) is the win: dense moving-512 base GEMM's per-instruction fp32 rate makes 3 bf16 products < fp32 emulation, and the bf16 limbs stay RESIDENT (same bytes as D1's fp32 lhs_t) so HBM read stays 2112MB (below D1's 2150, no per-M-tile fp32-weight reload trap) -- both swiglu-loss conditions absent (BL-20260710). Limb build/cast raised Vec 2->27% Scl 0->21% but hidden under PE (DMA idle 48%); HBM write byte-identical 201MB, no spill. 11.3034ms/1.297x = -23.8% vs same-session D1 (0.988x), gap far beyond ~1.3% jitter. Offline sim authorized (<1.3e-5) and Codex (high effort) confirmed the dilution 11.4x / quadrature / fail-closed args BEFORE the remote run. 3.4x faster than lora_v1 (38.36ms). PROMOTED; lora_v2_mblk4 (0.988x) kept as fp32 fallback. all_seeds_passed=False is the benign server allclose field NKIBench does not gate on.

D3 (make b resident across all M-blocks) MODEL-REJECT, per DEC-2 (no DMA/blocking gap in the D1/D2 profile to measure against). D2 is cleanly PE-bound: latency 11.30ms ~= TRUE PE-active 10.73ms (PE 95%), DMA idle at 47.6%. b is (R=128,N=12288) fp32 = 6.29MB; the current b_chunk [128,512] load-once-per-N-chunk over 24 chunks x 8 M-blocks = 50.3MB of reload; resident b would save 44.0MB = 2.09% of D2's 2111.6MB HBM read. Removing 2.1% of ALREADY-HIDDEN DMA read on a PE-bound op with DMA idle cannot move the wall (matches the matmul-family finding that amortizing hidden DMA does nothing when PE-bound). Also, resident b (24*512*4=48KB/part fp32) competes with D2's 80KB/part resident bf16 lhs limbs. Rejected on the model; datum recorded.
verdict: model-based-reject (D3 resident b; PE-bound, saves 2.09% hidden HBMrd)

notes: D4 (M-block factor sweep B in {2,8}) MODEL-REJECT, per DEC-2, carrying the sibling matmul finding on this IDENTICAL base GEMM: B=4 optimal, B=2 0.983x (under-amortized), B=8 full-run regressed 0.968x, B=16 0.519x (SBUF/PSUM pressure). lora's 2-level (m_hi,m_lo) index makes B=4 == m_lo the NATURAL arithmetic-free block (B=2/8 would require re-nesting m_hi/m_lo across the block boundary, more bug surface). PSUM: B=4 uses 4 acc banks [128,512] fp32 (of 8) + 1 transpose + 1 down-proj in the prologue = peak ~6; B=8 needs 8 acc banks (zero headroom) AND doubles D2's resident bf16 lhs limbs (2 limbs x B) -> exactly the pressure regime the sibling B=8 regressed on. B=2 halves DMA amortization while the op is already PE-bound with DMA hidden -> no upside. Rejected on the model + sibling evidence; datum recorded.
verdict: model-based-reject (D4 B-sweep {2,8}; sibling B=4 optimal, B=8 regressed)

notes: E2 (bf16x2 3-product split of the up-projection (x@a)@b) MODEL-REJECT. NUMERICALLY SAFE: offline route [B'] (base + up-proj split, down-proj fp32) composite rel-L2 = 4.438e-06 (runs/offline_lora_bf16_split_sim.py, seed 42) << 2e-5 gate. But NO PE UPSIDE: the up-proj is only 768 of D2's 97536 matmul instructions = 0.79% of the total; a bf16x2 3-product split cuts at most ~17% of the up-proj's PE = ~0.13% of total PE, an ORDER of magnitude below the ~1.3% measurement noise (BL-20260709-fast-vs-full-run-latency), while ADDING tT/b limb-build Vec/Scl ops. Rejected on the profile (below-noise gain for added work; the same sub-1%-PE-lever-below-noise reasoning as the sibling swiglu up/gate observations, BL-20260710-bf16x2-loses-when-fp32-emulates-in-2-passes). MOOT UNDER THE FOLD: lora_v4_fold (E1) removes the up-projection entirely (a@b folded into w'), so there is no up-proj left to split. Datum recorded; no remote spend.
verdict: model-based-reject (E2 up-proj split; 0.13% of total PE, below noise; moot under the fold)

disposition: model-based reject (not built; SBUF pre-gate + measured sibling precedent)
notes: E3 (double-buffer the lhs bf16 limbs to close D2's ~5.0% / 0.569 ms PE-idle bubble) MODEL-REJECT on the offline SBUF pre-gate (AC-4.3) + measured sibling precedent. The 0.569 ms bubble is the per-m_hi-block prologue (transpose + down-proj + limb build) that cannot overlap that block's own N-loop (the N-loop consumes the limbs); closing it needs cross-block overlap => double-buffered lhs limbs. SBUF BUDGET: 2x resident bf16 lhs limbs at B=4 (each limb [B=4,K_TILES=40,128,128] bf16 = 40*128*2*4 = 40960 B/part = 40 KB/part; two limbs 80 KB; DOUBLE-BUFFERED = 160 KB) + a_local 20 KB + tT 2 KB + per-chunk w transients ~12 KB = ~194 KB/partition > the 192 KB trn2 SBUF limit BEFORE compiler temporaries => predicted HARD SPILL (the tmm_v7_dbuf_rhs read-floor-break signature). MEASURED SIBLING PRECEDENT (not projected): the identical double-buffer lever was BUILT and measured-rejected on TWO siblings -- tmm_v7_dbuf_rhs (transpose_matmul phase 3) engaged its intended prefetch overlap (~0.2% PE dip) but BROKE the AC-4 read floor (hbm_read 229->283 MB +23.8%) + a small write-spill (+2.1%), see BL-20260711-wider-limb-build-chunk-spills-is-doublebuffer-proxy; bmm phase 3 found cross-block blocking a MONOTONE anti-lever (enlarged live set constrains the affine_range pipeline), BL-20260710-cross-batch-blocking-is-an-antilever-on-affine-range. The ceiling here is only the 5% idle gap, and even a WORKING prefetch on the sibling recovered a sub-adopt-bar sliver before AC-4 rejected it. Build only as a contingency IFF the fold finalizes to D2 AND a re-derived SBUF budget shows real headroom below 192 KB with margin (it does not). Datum recorded; not built.
verdict: model-based-reject (E3 double-buffer lhs limbs; ~194 KB/part > 192 KB predicted spill + measured tmm/bmm double-buffer rejects)

disposition: measured reject (WASH; the extra HBM round-trip does not pay)
structure: Weight-fold: out = x@w + (x@a)@b == x@(w + a@b) == x@w'. Prologue (SEPARATE RAW pass, fully materializes w' to fp32 HBM before any main-GEMM read): aT[kt]=transpose(v3[kt])=[R,k_in] resident (identity idiom); per kt (40) x N-chunk c (24 of 512): ab_chunk = nc_matmul(aT[kt] [R,k_in], b_chunk [R,512]) = a[kt]@b[:,cols] = [k_in,512] fp32 PSUM; w_prime[kt,:,cols] = v2[kt,:,cols] + ab_chunk (fp32 add, STORE fp32 to HBM, an internal shared_hbm (40,128,12288) scratch). Main loop = sibling matmul_v3_bf16_split on w' (down-proj/up-proj/resident-a/tT DELETED): per m_hi B=4 M-block build resident bf16 lhs limbs; per N-chunk c per kt load w'[kt,:,cols] fp32 + split -> w'_hi/w'_lo bf16 (split ONLY at consumption, w' stays fp32 in HBM); per m_lo acc += lhs_hi@w'_hi + lhs_hi@w'_lo + lhs_lo@w'_hi (3-product, drop lo@lo); 512-wide 4-sub-tile store. Guards: w'-fp32-in-HBM (bf16 w' would route the 99.6%-dominant low-rank through one rounding -> ~2.3e-3 FAIL); separate-pass RAW (no speculative consume).
notes: E1, the phase-3 weight-fold candidate -- MEASURED REJECT (wash), the definitive test of the canonical LoRA trick + the phase-1 prompt's low-rank-fusion hint on real hardware. AC-2 offline gate AUTHORIZED before spend: fold route [F] seed-42 4.450e-6, diversity worst 4.456e-6 (< 8e-6 model-consistency < 1.3e-5 cap), fp32 reassociation control [F-fp32] 6.079e-7 (~1.25x fp32 floor, ~7.3x below the bf16 fold -> folded error is bf16-DOMINATED not a reassociation artifact); Codex (high effort) AGREED all 4 numeric points. AC-1: on-device full-5-seed PASS rel-L2 4.4484e-6 all seeds == offline fold 4.450e-6 == predicted quadrature 4.476e-6 (~4.5x under gate); bf16 DOMINATES (INVERTS D2's fp32-floor-dominated 6.240e-7 because the fold LOSES the 11.4x low-rank dilution -- the whole output flows through one bf16x2 GEMM). AC-3: same-session interleaved A/B D2-before 11.2992 / E1 11.1756 / D2-after 11.2986 (band 0.0006ms); E1 beats faster D2 by 0.123ms = 1.09% << max(band, 0.34ms=3%) bar -> WASH, NOT promoted. AC-4: HBMwr 201->453MB (+252 = intentional w' materialization, band exact <=500, NO spill), HBMrd 2112->2297MB (+8.8%, <=2600, NO re-fetch/spill), matmul_instr 97536->95400, psum 2080->1098. MECHANISM: TRUE PE-active 10.7351->10.6548ms (-0.75%: the fold DOES remove the low-rank-tail PE) but the a@b materialization PE is ADDITIVE on a PE-bound op and the +252MB w' write + +186MB read only partially hide under DMA idle -> net wall only -1.12%, a wash. The 14.6645/10.656=1.376x ceiling was correctly demoted to an unreachable theoretical bound (assumes zero materialization cost). CONCLUSION: the extra HBM round-trip does not pay for the tail removal; D2's PSUM-fused fp32 low-rank (no HBM round-trip, byte-identical HBMwr 201MB) is strictly better. FINALIZE D2 at 1.297x; lora_v4_fold recorded as a measured reject. all_seeds_passed=False is the benign server allclose field NKIBench does not gate on. AC-5 CAVEAT: all 5 on-device seeds draw the seed-42 input (adapter reseeds np.random.seed(42)); the true distinct-input margin is the offline diversity worst 4.456e-6 (seeds 0/21/63/84).
verdict: measured-reject-WASH (weight-fold 1.312x vs D2 1.298x same-session, 1.09% < 3% bar; extra HBM round-trip does not pay)
